Court No. - 74
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 30094 of 2024
Applicant :- Mohd Nadeem

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Mohit Kumar Singh,Sujata Choudhary
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Satyam Narayan
Hon'ble Saurabh Shyam Shamshery,J.
1.

Heard Ms. Sujata Choudhary, learned counsel for applicant and Mr. Satyam Narayan, learned
counsel for complainant.

2.  The present bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed on behalf of applicant to release him on bail in Case Crime No. 725 of 2022, under Sections 302, 323, 506, 201, 498A I.P.C and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station- Lisadi, District- Meerut.
3.
This is third bail application filed on behalf of applicant.

First bail application was rejected by a reasoned order dated 02.05.2023 and relevant part of the same is reproduced hereinafter:-
Mohd Nadeem vs State Of U.P. on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182180281/

sentences.text: In the backdrop of above referred submissions and facts of present case, it transpires that victim has died under other than normal circumstances after 11 years and 5 months of her marriage.
Conduct of husband of deceased and his family members was under cloud of doubt since despite being unnatural death, they have not informed the police and buried her.

12. It also transpires that burial took place in presence of relatives of deceased,
however, later on, on basis of allegations made in F.I.R., dead body was exhumed and according to post mortem, it was a case of strangulation with thyroid and trachea bone were found fractured.
Therefore, all the accused persons including applicants herein have prima facie committed a case of disappearance of evidence.

13. Senior Advocate for applicants has placed heavy reliance on confessional statement of husband of deceased who have been attributed entire occurrence on himself only, with further submission that there was a dispute between deceased and her husband in regard to allegations of extra-marital affairs of her husband, however,
there is an evidence of daughter of deceased, who has implicated all accused persons including both applicants herein, that not only they were present at the place of occurrence but assaulted her mother also.

14. Senior Advocate has put doubt on above referred evidence of daughter of deceased on two grounds, firstly, she was usually staying at her nana's home as well as her statement was recorded after two months, however, the said factors may not be an adverse effect on evidence of girl.

Since there is no reason for her to forcefully implicate all family members as well as only on ground that there was a delay in recording statement of said witness, its evidentiary value cannot be considered to be less.

It is also not improbable that such girl was present at the house, therefore,
considering conduct of applicants that they have not informed the police about unnatural death as well as that body was later on exhumed and it was found to be prima facie a case of murder and coupled with the fact that at this stage, there is no material before this Court to doubt the evidence of 11 years old girl (daughter of deceased), no case of bail is made out.

15. Both bail applications are accordingly rejected."
4. The second bail application was rejected by following order dated 16.08.2023:-
"Bail application is rejected.
For reasons, see order of date passed in Bail Application No. 35662 of 2023."

5. The aforesaid order was challenged by way of filing of a SLP Criminal No. 16289 of 2023 before Supreme Court, however, it was disposed of, vide order dated 08.01.2024, without interfering with the impugned order with a liberty to the petitioner therein to renew the application for bail after a Mohd Nadeem vs State Of U.P. on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182180281/

time. This application is being filed on 26.07.2023 i.e. after six months of the above referred order.

6. In pursuance of order dated 14.08.2024 passed by this Court learned trial court has submitted a status report that out of the proposed 15 witnesses 3 have already been examined and the trial could be concluded within a period of one year.

7. Learned counsel for applicant submits that meanwhile bail applications of two co-accused namely Jaan Mohammad and Jakrunisha @ Jakrunnisha have been allowed and they have been granted bail by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 03.10.2023.
Though she fairly submits that the orders passed by this Court were not placed before the co-ordinate Bench.

Learned counsel further submits that in statements recorded during the trial no specific allegation has been assigned to the present applicant and for that she referred few paragraphs of the statements of the witnesses recorded during the course of trial.
8. The aforesaid submissions are opposed by learned counsel for complainant.

9. At this stage, to consider the testimony in detail as referred above the only subsequent events for consideration of this third bail application are that 2 co-accused have already been granted bail by co-ordinate Bench of this Court, though the order of this Court was not placed before the co-ordinate Bench as well as that the status of trial was also not brought on record.

The second subsequent event is to consider the statement of the witnesses recorded during the trial so much as that no allegation was made against the present applicant in regard to offence of murder.

The Court takes note that the applicant is elder brother of husband of deceased there is not much opposition to a a submission that in the statement of PW-3, no specific role has been assigned to the applicant that he was involved in the offence of murder.

In the aforesaid circumstances, considering the overall circumstances of the case as well as that applicant is in jail since 22.01.2023 i.e. for about more than one and a half years and that trial may take some more time and there is no material that the applicant may influence any witnesses since testimony of 3 material witnesses has already been concluded, therefore, the applicant has made out a case for bail.

10. Let the applicant- Mohd Nadeem, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment or exemption from appearance on the date fixed in trial.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

sentences.text: (iii) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.

In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.

(iv) The Trial Court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously, preferably within a period of six months after release of applicant,
if there is no other legal impediment.
(v) Applicant has to appear on each and every date before learned trial Court and any application for exemption of his appearance on vague ground could be a ground for cancellation of bail by learned trial Court immediately.
11. The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
12.
The bail application is allowed.
13. It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only for the purpose of adjudicating the present bail application.
